title: NVIDIA: What Really Happened Behind Closed Doors Between November 11 and November 23?
gist: Kalar Rajendiran lays out a chronology of NVIDIA's November 2026 CEO turmoil (Huang resigns Nov 11–12, CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO, chairman reaffirms Nov 17, Reuters reports SEC accounting scrutiny Nov 20, Huang unanimously reinstated Nov 23). He floats an explicitly unproven hypothesis: Kress may have reconsidered the interim role after learning of the SEC probe, leaving the board with reinstating Huang as the easiest option.

insights.claim: NVIDIA's board unanimously accepted Jensen Huang's resignation on November 11–12, 2026 and appointed long-serving CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Establishes the baseline governance timeline for assessing NVDA leadership risk.
insights.locator: November 11–12: Huang resigns; Kress takes over.

insights.claim: On November 17, 2026 NVIDIA chairman Harvey Jones publicly reaffirmed that Huang would not be reinstated, endorsed Kress's leadership, and confirmed a permanent CEO search was underway.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: The board reversed a publicly reaffirmed position within six days, a governance-credibility red flag.
insights.locator: November 17: The board reinforces its decision.

insights.claim: NVIDIA reported a blowout quarter with strong forward guidance on its November 17, 2026 earnings call, so there was no publicly apparent operational crisis requiring an immediate CEO change.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Strong fundamentals mean the CEO reversal was driven by non-operational factors, which is what investors need to understand.
insights.quote: There is no publicly apparent operational crisis requiring an immediate change of CEO.

insights.claim: NVIDIA's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on November 23, 2026, reversing its decision days after reaffirming it; the author stresses all ten directors reversed.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: A unanimous abrupt reversal raises questions about board independence relevant to governance-focused holders.

insights.claim: Reuters reported on November 20, 2026 that SEC enforcement staff are examining NVIDIA's accounting practices, including financial arrangements with AI customers.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Customer-financing arrangements in AI (vendor financing of buyers) are a key revenue-quality risk to monitor for NVDA.
insights.locator: November 20: SEC accounting scrutiny becomes public.

insights.claim: Reuters had previously reported disagreements between Kress and Huang over certain NVIDIA customer-financing arrangements that are now part of the SEC's accounting scrutiny.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: A CFO-CEO split over customer financing is a classic revenue-recognition warning sign worth tracking in filings.

insights.claim: NVIDIA stock fell harder in a single day on November 20 on news of the SEC investigation than it did during Huang's resignation and week-plus absence from November 12 to 19, per the author.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: The market priced accounting risk above key-person risk, suggesting the SEC probe is the larger overhang for NVDA.
insights.quote: the stock dropped much harder in a single day (on Nov. 20) on news of the SEC investigation than it did when Jensen resigned

insights.claim: The author hypothesizes that Colette Kress may have reconsidered remaining NVIDIA interim CEO after learning of the SEC investigation and its financial, regulatory and personal responsibilities, leaving the board a succession dilemma that reinstating Huang conveniently resolved.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: If true, NVDA's leadership reversal is tied to the accounting probe, raising its severity; watch for disclosures on Kress's role and the SEC matter.
insights.quote: And did reinstating Huang become the most convenient way out?

insights.claim: The author argues an external CEO search for NVIDIA would have become considerably more complicated amid mounting accounting and governance scrutiny.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Regulatory overhangs can constrain succession options and entrench incumbent leaders, increasing key-person dependence.

insights.claim: The author explicitly does not allege that Kress asked to leave, that the SEC probe triggered Huang's reinstatement, or that the NVIDIA board acted improperly, describing these as hypotheses requiring evidence.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Treat the Kress-SEC linkage as speculation, not reported fact, when sizing NVDA governance risk.
insights.locator: To be clear: I am not alleging

insights.claim: The author argues the key unanswered question is what changed inside NVIDIA between November 17 and November 22, listing questions such as when Kress learned of the SEC probe and whether the probe featured in board succession deliberations.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Future reporting or proxy/8-K disclosures on board deliberations in this window could move NVDA.
insights.quote: It is what happened inside NVIDIA between November 17 and November 22.
